items.title: Dave Rivello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012
items.q: I think it’s Frank Foster — “Blues in Hoss Flat,” and that’s one of the best things ever.

ctx.x: Okay. What about something classic? “Shiny Stockings” or those kind of things. Is that a different — I can’t finish the question really but, it’s another era.

I think understanding that part of things is important. And I believe that anything that the Count Basie Orchestra did, I think you have to just know that. You have to be able to feel that. You have to have listened to it so much that it’s part of you. And my favorite, probably, Count Basie album is “Chairman of the Board.” And Thad Jones wrote some of the arrangements and Frank Foster’s — I think it’s Frank Foster — “Blues in Hoss Flat,” and that’s one of the best things ever. And lots of people know that…

wrote very strange modern classical music — what people would term strange — but I mean very avante garde, still somehow Basie was in there. And I think that that feeling and that band has to go with anybody who’s serious about this music.
